chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halabi, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "And no leaf falls except that He knows it, and no grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor any moist, nor any dry, except that it is in a clear Book." He said: Then he said: The leaf is the miscarried fetus, the grain is the child, the darknesses of the earth are the wombs, the moist is that which lives, and the dry is that which is not perfected. And all of that is in a clear Book.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'leaf', 'grain', and 'darknesses of the earth' in Surah Al-An'am?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Abu Basir reports Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) specific exegesis of Quran 6:59, interpreting the 'leaf' as a miscarried fetus and the 'grain' as a born child. The scholar elucidates that the 'darknesses of the earth' symbolize the wombs, while 'moist' and 'dry' denote the stages of life and development, respectively. This interpretation underscores the comprehensive nature of divine knowledge, affirming that every stage of human existence, from conception to birth, is meticulously recorded in the 'clear book' (Kitab Mubin).
